column1: truculence§Truculence in a first meeting usually means fear of the second.§初次见面的**粗野**，通常意味着对第二次的恐惧。
trustworthy§A trustworthy narrator is a choice the author makes.§**可靠**的叙述者是作者作出的一个选择。
tryst§What the diary calls a tryst the letters call a lecture.§日记里称为**幽会**的，信里叫作讲座。
tumultuous§The century was tumultuous and the parish records are calm.§这个世纪**动荡不安**，教区记录却平静如常。
turmoil§Turmoil in the market is an opportunity for exactly two people.§市场的**动荡**对恰好两个人来说是机会。
turpitude§Turpitude is a word that survives only in legal forms.§“**卑劣**”这个词只在法律文书里留存下来。
tyrannical§A tyrannical proofreader is a writer's best friend.§一个**暴君般**的校对员是作者最好的朋友。
tyranny§The tyranny of small tasks is what eats a research week.§琐事的**暴政**吞掉了一整周的研究时间。
tyrant§Every tyrant in the record was somebody's competent administrator.§记录里的每个**暴君**，都曾是某些人眼中称职的管理者。
ubiquitous§The word became ubiquitous within a year of the film.§这个词在电影上映一年内就**随处可见**了。
unacquainted§I am unacquainted with the second edition and cannot judge it.§我**不熟悉**第二版，无法评判。
unadorned§Unadorned brick was a decision, not a shortage of money.§**裸露**的清水砖是一个选择，而不是缺钱。
unaffected§He was unaffected by the criticism and changed nothing.§他**不为批评所动**，什么也没改。
unalterable§Nothing about the schedule is unalterable except the tide.§这份日程表上除了潮汐，**没有什么不能改**。
unanticipated§An unanticipated benefit was that the room became quiet.§一个**意想不到**的好处是房间变安静了。
unappreciated§Unappreciated work is not the same as unimportant work.§**不被赏识**的工作与不重要的工作不是一回事。
unapproachable§An unapproachable standard makes everyone give up early.§一个**高不可攀**的标准会让所有人早早放弃。
unassuming§An unassuming building holds the best collection in the county.§一栋**不起眼**的建筑藏着全郡最好的收藏。
unattainable§Perfection is unattainable and useful as a direction.§完美**无法达到**，作为方向却有用。
unattractive§An unattractive option can still be the right one.§一个**没有吸引力**的选项仍可能是正确的。
unavoidable§Some redundancy is unavoidable and most of it is not.§有些冗余**不可避免**，大部分则可以避免。
unaware§We remain unaware of most of what shapes us.§塑造我们的东西，我们大多**毫无察觉**。
unbounded§An unbounded problem has no solution worth computing.§**无界**的问题没有值得计算的解。
uncensored§The uncensored version is duller than the rumour promised.§**未删节版**比传言说的要乏味。
unchanged§The essentials are unchanged; only the packaging moved.§**实质没变**，只是包装换了。
unchanging§An unchanging landscape is usually one that is being managed.§一成**不变的**景观通常是被人为维护的。
unconcerned§Unconcerned about fashion, the design has outlasted three.§这个设计**不理会**潮流，已经熬过了三轮时尚。
unconditional§Unconditional support is rarely as useful as it sounds.§**无条件**的支持很少像听起来那么有用。
unconscionable§It would be unconscionable to charge for a correction.§为一次更正收费是**不合情理**的。
undaunted§Undaunted by the weather, they finished the survey in fog.§他们**不为天气所阻**，在雾中完成了勘测。
underscore§A single underscore in the margin marked the crucial line.§页边一道**下划线**标出了关键的那一行。
undesirable§Being described as undesirable ended his career quite legally.§被描述为“**不受欢迎**的人”，完全合法地终结了他的事业。
unequivocal§Unequivocal language is the hardest thing to write under pressure.§在压力下最难写的就是毫**不含糊**的文字。
uneven§Uneven paving is the most common cause of falls here.§**不平整**的铺装是这里最常见的跌倒原因。
unexpectedness§Half the effect of the ending is its unexpectedness.§这个结局一半的效果来自它的**出乎意料**。
unflappable§Unflappable is a reputation that takes one crisis to earn.§“**临危不乱**”的名声，一次危机就能挣得。
unforeseen§Every budget has a line for the unforeseen and it is too small.§每份预算都有一项“**不可预见**费”，而且总是太少。
ungainly§An ungainly first attempt is the price of a graceful second.§第一次的**笨拙**，是第二次优雅的代价。
unhinge§The door unhinged itself in the wind and hit the wall.§门在风中**脱了铰链**，撞上了墙。
uniformity§Uniformity is useful for boxes and dangerous for people.§**统一**对箱子有用，对人却危险。
unintelligible§Handwriting unintelligible to us was ordinary to his clerk.§我们**看不懂**的笔迹，对他的书吏来说很平常。
unique§Almost nothing is unique; most things are merely rare.§几乎没有什么是**独一无二的**，多数只是稀有。
unjust§An unjust rule that is never enforced is still unjust.§一条从未被执行的**不公**规则仍然是不公的。
unleash§Unleashing the dogs on the beach is forbidden in summer.§夏天禁止在沙滩上**放开狗绳**。
unlikely§An unlikely hero is the only kind worth writing about.§**不像英雄**的英雄，才是唯一值得写的。
unlimited§Unlimited access sounds generous and produces nothing.§**无限**制的使用权听起来慷慨，却什么也产不出。
unmediated§There is no unmediated view of the past.§对过去不存在**不经中介**的观看。
unnatural§An unnatural silence in the wood means a hawk is near.§林中**反常的**寂静意味着有鹰在附近。
unnecessary§Unnecessary precision is a way of avoiding a decision.§**不必要的**精确是一种逃避决定的方式。
unobtainable§The part is unobtainable and the machine still runs.§这个零件已经**买不到**，机器却还在转。
unorthodox§An unorthodox route up the hill turned out to be the old one.§一条**非正统的**上山路线原来才是老路。
unpalatable§Unpalatable advice is the only kind worth paying for.§**难以下咽**的建议才是唯一值得花钱买的。
unparalleled§An unparalleled run of dry summers ended in 1976.§一连串**前所未有**的干燥夏天在一九七六年结束。
unpopular§The unpopular chapter is the one people remember.§那一章**不受欢迎**，却是人们记住的一章。
unprecedented§Unprecedented is a word to check before using.§“**史无前例**”是个用之前要核对的词。
unpredictable§Unpredictable is not the same as random.§**不可预测**与随机不是一回事。
unpretentious§An unpretentious meal at a plain table was the best of the trip.§一顿在**朴素**桌上的简单饭菜是全程最好的。
unprincipled§An unprincipled shortcut saved a week and cost the archive.§一条毫**无原则的**捷径省了一周，却毁了档案。
unproductive§An unproductive week is often the one that makes the next possible.§**毫无产出**的一周，往往成全了接下来的一周。
unqualified§I give it my unqualified support and one small reservation.§我给予它**毫无保留**的支持，外加一点小小的保留意见。
unrealistic§An unrealistic deadline produces work that has to be redone.§**不切实际**的截止日期造出的东西还得重做。
unrealized§Unrealized gains are not money until they are sold.§**未实现**的收益在卖出之前不算钱。
unrelenting§Unrelenting politeness can be a form of distance.§**毫不松懈**的礼貌可能是一种距离。
unruly§Unruly hair and an orderly mind, said the obituary.§讣告写道：头发**乱蓬蓬**，脑子井井有条。
unscrupulous§Unscrupulous is what we call ambition on the other side.§我们把对方的野心称作**不择手段**。
unseen§The unseen work is what makes the visible work possible.§**看不见的**工作，成全了看得见的工作。
unsettle§A good question should unsettle the person who asks it.§一个好问题应当先**动摇**提问者本人。
unstable§An unstable compound has to be made where it is used.§**不稳定**的化合物必须在使用地点现制。
